poems.title: 春の日の夕暮
poems.author: 中原中也

vocabulary.gloss: losing, having lost (historical kana for 失い)
if (I) say (historical kana for 言えば)

poems.paraphrase:
トタン屋根がせんべいを食べていて、春の日の夕暮れは穏やかだ。下から投げられた灰が青白くなって、春の日の夕暮れは静かだ。
ああ、かかしはないだろうか。たぶんないだろう。馬はいななくだろうか。いななきもしないだろう。月の光がぬるりと広がるのにただ任せて、おとなしく従っているのは春の日の夕暮れなのだろうか。
野原の中に寺の建物がぽつんと赤く見える。荷馬車の車輪は油が切れている。私が「歴史的現在」で何か言うと、空と山があざ笑う。
瓦が一枚、はずれて落ちた。これから春の日の夕暮れは、黙ったまま前へ進んでいく。自分自身の静脈の中へと進んでいくのだ。
poems.gloss: The tin roof eats a rice cracker, and the evening of the spring day is calm. Ash thrown underhand turns pale, and the evening of the spring day is quiet. Ah, is there no scarecrow? There will be none. Does a horse neigh? It will not neigh either. Simply letting the moonlight spread in its slippery way, is it the spring evening that is so obedient? Out in the fields a temple stands red, the wheels of a horse cart have lost their oil, and when I say something in the historical present, the sky and the mountains mock me, mock me. One roof tile has come loose. From now on the spring evening, without a word, will advance - into its own veins.
poems.note: A Dada-influenced poem built from deliberately odd images (a tin roof eating a rice cracker, the evening moving into its own veins); many lines have no single literal meaning, so the paraphrase keeps them as they are. Note historical kana (失ひ = 失い, 云へば = 言えば) and the negative guess 〜まい (あるまい 'there probably is none').

poems.title: 春
poems.author: 山村暮鳥

vocabulary.gloss: to go (literary form of 行く)
to chase after (small っ written as full つ)

poems.paraphrase: のろいなあ、のろいなあ。菜の花の畑の中を走っていく汽車は。ひらひら、ひらひらと、その汽車のあとから追いかけていくチョウがいる。
poems.gloss: How slow, how slow is the train going through the fields of rapeseed flowers. Flutter, flutter, flu-utter: behind it, a butterfly chases that train.
poems.note: The repeated ひら / ひいら imitates a butterfly's fluttering, and the joke is that the train is so slow a butterfly can keep up with it. 蝶々 was written てふてふ in historical kana, and 追つかける uses a full-size つ for the small っ.

poems.title: 春の夕暮
poems.author: 中原中也

vocabulary.gloss: if (I) say (historical kana for 言えば)

poems.paraphrase:
塗った板がせんべいを食べていて、春の日の夕暮れは静かだ。
下から投げられた灰が青白くなって、春の日の夕暮れは穏やかだ。
ああ、かかしはないだろうか。たぶんないだろう。馬はいななくだろうか。いななきもしないだろう。青い月の光がぬるりと広がるのにただ任せて、おとなしく従っているのは春の日の夕暮れなのだろうか。
野原の中の寺の建物が、ろうそくのしずくに照らされるように、ぽつんと赤く見える。荷馬車の車輪は油が切れている。私が「歴史的現在」で何か言うと、空と山があざ笑う。
瓦が一枚、はずれて落ちた。春の日の夕暮れは、これから黙ったまま前へ進んでいく。自分自身の静脈の中へと進んでいくのだ。
poems.gloss: The painted board eats a rice cracker, and the evening of the spring day is quiet. Ash thrown underhand turns pale, and the evening of the spring day is calm. Ah, is there no scarecrow? There will be none. Does a horse neigh? It will not neigh either. Simply letting the blue moonlight spread in its slippery way, is it the spring evening that is so obedient? Out in the fields, the temple stands red among drops of candle wax; the wheels of the horse cart have lost their oil, and when I say something in the historical present, the sky and the mountains mock me, mock me. One roof tile has come loose. From now on the spring evening, without a word, will advance - into its own veins.
poems.note: An earlier variant of 春の日の夕暮, with small differences (塗板 for トタン, the added 臘涙 'wax tears', 青色の月の光). The imagery is surreal on purpose, and the phrase ポトホトと臘涙に has no clear literal sense, so the paraphrase of that line is only approximate.

poems.title: 旅上
poems.author: 萩原朔太郎

vocabulary.gloss: wheat or barley (old form of 麦)
sorrow, melancholy (historical kana for うれい)
means, way to live or to go (literary)
ah; sad, moving (historical kana for あわれ)

poems.paraphrase:
かすんだ空の下で麦の穂が流れるように揺れ、麦が揺れている。
悲しみをのせて汽車は走っていく。
どう生きればいいのかもわからないまま、
私が食べる麦の青さから、
ああ、はるか遠くへ、
空を流れるようにして汽車は走っていく。
poems.gloss: Under a hazy sky the wheat flows, the wheat flows, and the train goes on carrying sorrow. Not knowing how to live, away from the green of the grain I eat, ah, far, far off, the train goes flowing through the sky.
poems.note: A melancholy travel image: wheat rippling like water and a train carrying the speaker's sorrow. 知らに is a classical negative ('without knowing'), たづき means a way or means of living, and the line わが喰むむぎの蒼さより can be read as 'from' or 'more than' the green of the grain, so the paraphrase keeps it simple.

poems.title: 初夏
poems.author: 中原中也

vocabulary.gloss: to begin to long for / fall in love

poems.paraphrase:
扇子と香水。
君、新聞紙は絹のふろしきに包んだかい。
夕方の月が風の中を泳いでいる。
アメリカの国旗とソーダ水が
恋しくなり始める季節だね。
poems.gloss: A folding fan and perfume. Did you wrap the newspaper in the silk wrapping cloth? The evening moon swims in the wind. It is the season when the American flag and soda water start to fall in love.
poems.note: A light sketch of early-summer things (fan, perfume, soda water). The last lines are ambiguous: they can mean the flag and soda water begin to 'fall in love', or that people begin to long for them, so the renderings stay close to the wording.

poems.title: 夏
poems.author: 北原白秋
poems.paraphrase: 手前に一本のアシがある。遠くには富士山がある。そのアシは、富士山よりもさらに高く、みずみずしく風にそよいでいる。近くのものが遠くの山より大きく見える、夏の景色だ。
poems.gloss: In the foreground, a single reed; in the distance, Mount Fuji. Higher even than Fuji, the reed rustles, fresh.
poems.note: The poem plays with perspective: a reed close by looks taller than distant Fuji. It is written in kanji with katakana okurigana, and 戦ゲリ uses the classical completion/continuation auxiliary り ('is rustling').

poems.title: 蝉
poems.author: 中原中也

vocabulary.gloss: is singing (historical kana for 鳴いている)
to say (historical kana for 言う)

poems.paraphrase:
セミが鳴いている、セミが鳴いている。セミが鳴いているほかには何もない。僕はうとうとしている。少し風もある。松林のすきまから空が見える。僕はうとうとしている。
「いや、そうじゃない、そうじゃない」と彼が言う。「違っているよ」と僕が言う。「いや、いや」と彼が言う。「違っているよ」と僕が言う。そこで目が覚める。彼はもうずっと前に死んだやつなのだ。それから、彼が眠っている墓場のことなどが目に浮かぶ。
それは中国地方のある田舎の、水無河原という川のそばだ。雨の日以外は水がない、伝説のある川のほとりで、やぶのかげの砂地にある小さな墓場だ。そこでもセミは鳴いているだろう。夕日もちらちら差しているだろう。
セミが鳴いている、セミが鳴いている。セミが鳴いているほかには何もない。
僕は怠けているのか。僕は「怠け者」なのか。僕は自分のことを何とも思わない。
セミが鳴いている、セミが鳴いている。セミが鳴いているほかには何もない。
poems.gloss: Cicadas are singing, cicadas are singing; there is nothing but cicadas singing. I doze off. There is a little wind, too. The sky shows through the pine grove. I doze off. 'No, that's not it, that's not it!' he says. 'You've got it wrong,' I say. 'No, no!' he says. 'You've got it wrong,' I say. And then I wake up, and he is someone who died long ago. Then the graveyard where he lies in his eternal sleep comes to mind. It is in a village somewhere in the Chugoku region, by a river called the Mizunashi-gawara, which has water only on rainy days and has a legend attached to it: a small graveyard of sandy soil in the shade of a thicket. Cicadas must be singing there too, and the evening sun must be flickering on it. Cicadas are singing; there is nothing but cicadas singing. My laziness? Am I 'lazy'? I think nothing at all of myself. Cicadas are singing; there is nothing but cicadas singing.
poems.note: A summer daydream in which the drone of cicadas brings back a dead friend and his grave; 中国 here means the Chugoku region of western Japan, not China. Watch the historical kana: ゐる = いる, さうぢやない = そうじゃない, ちがつて = ちがって, 思はぬ = 思わない.

poems.title: 夏と私
poems.author: 中原中也

vocabulary.gloss: the path one has come; one's past

poems.paraphrase:
真っ白な嘆きの中で、海を見た。カモメを見た。
高いところから、風のまっただ中で、思い出のかけらがひるがえるのを見た。
夏になると、高い山に、真っ白な嘆きを見た。
燃えるように暑い山道を登っていき、頂上の風に吹かれた。
風に吹かれながら、自分が歩いてきた道をふり返って、ぼうぜんとした。そして泣いた。
果てしのないその心を、母にも、もちろん友だちにも打ち明けなかった。
それでも望みだけはあって、腕を組んだまま何もできず、その望みに押しつぶされる。
そんな自分の姿を見た。夏になると、そのような自分の姿を見た。
poems.gloss: In a pure white lamenting, I saw the sea, I saw the gulls. From on high, in the midst of the wind, I saw fragments of memory tumbling. When summer came, on the high mountains I saw a pure white grief. Climbing the burning mountain path, I was blown by the wind at the summit. Blown by the wind, I stood stunned before the way I had come, and I wept. That endless heart I revealed neither to my mother nor, of course, to my friends. And yet, having only hope, I stood with folded arms and was overwhelmed by that hope. I saw myself; when summer came, I saw myself like that.
poems.note: Written in a classical style: 〜たり and 〜ぬ mark completed actions (見たり 'saw', 涙しぬ 'wept'), 〜ざりき is a past negative, そが means その, and 夏としなれば means 'when summer comes'. The mood is lonely youthful longing that cannot be shared.

poems.title: 夏の日の歌
poems.author: 中原中也

vocabulary.gloss: touchingly, pitiably dear (historical kana for いじらしく)

poems.paraphrase:
青い空は動かない。雲のかけらも一つもない。夏の真昼の静けさの中では、タールの光さえきれいに見える。
夏の空には何かがある。いじらしく思わせる何かがある。焼けたように色の濃い、太くてたくましいひまわりが、田舎の駅に咲いている。
子どもを上手に育てていく母親のように、汽車の汽笛が鳴る。山の近くを走るときに。
山の近くを走りながら、母親のように汽車の汽笛が鳴る。夏の真昼の暑いときに。
poems.gloss: The blue sky does not move; there is not a single scrap of cloud. In the stillness of a summer noon even the shine of the tar becomes clean. In the summer sky there is something, something that makes you feel a tender ache. Scorched and sturdy sunflowers are blooming at a country station. Like a mother who raises her children well, the train's whistle sounds - when it runs near the mountains. Running near the mountains, like a mother, the train's whistle sounds - at the hot hour of a summer noon.
poems.note: A still, bright noon scene; the unusual simile compares the train whistle to a capable, caring mother. Historical kana: いぢらしく = いじらしく, 思はせる = 思わせる, 咲いてゐる = 咲いている; 雲片 is read くもぎれ.

poems.title: 秋の日曜
poems.author: 中原中也

vocabulary.gloss: do not warm to each other
to feel fondness for old times

poems.paraphrase:
私の部屋の窓から見えるのは、空の広告だ。軽く上がった二つの気球だ。
青い空は金色に澄んでいて、そこからきのこの香りが生まれ、娘が生まれ、夢も生まれる。
でも風は冷たくなり、町は全体に雨の次の日のようで、初めて紹介された人どうしは打ち解けない。
だれもが再会をなつかしんでいる。あのおとなしい奥さんも、昔の喜びを思い出して笑い出す。
poems.gloss: From my room, through the window, I can see an air sign: two balloons that have risen lightly. The blue sky is clear and golden; from it the scent of mushrooms is born, girls are born, and dreams are born too. Yet the wind has turned cold, the whole town feels like the day after rain, and people introduced for the first time do not warm to each other. Everyone is fond of reunions; even that faithful, gentle wife breaks into laughter at old joys.
poems.note: エヤ・サイン is 'air sign', advertising balloons floating over the town. Historical kana: あがつた = あがった, いつたいに ('on the whole') = いったいに, やうで = ようで, 笑ひいでる = 笑い出る ('break into laughter').

poems.title: 一つのメルヘン
poems.author: 中原中也

vocabulary.gloss: is shining (historical kana for 射している)

poems.paraphrase:
秋の夜、はるか遠くに、小石ばかりの河原があって、そこに日の光がさらさらと差していた。
日の光といっても、まるで石英か何かのようで、とても固いものの粉のようだった。だからこそ、さらさらと、かすかな音も立てていた。
さて、小石の上に、今ちょうど一匹のチョウがとまり、うすいけれどもはっきりした影を落としていた。
やがてそのチョウが見えなくなると、いつのまにか、それまで流れていなかった川底に、水がさらさらと流れていた。
poems.gloss: On an autumn night, far, far away, there was a riverbed of nothing but pebbles, and on it the sun was shining, rustle, rustle. Though I call it sunlight, it was like silica or something, like the powder of some extremely hard substance, and that is why it was making a faint rustling sound. Then, on a pebble, a butterfly had just alighted, casting a shadow that was faint and yet sharply outlined. Soon, when the butterfly could no longer be seen, before anyone knew it, water was flowing, rustle, rustle, in the riverbed where nothing had flowed until then.
poems.note: A dreamlike scene in which sunlight shines at night and a dry riverbed quietly fills with water; さらさら repeats as both the sound of dry powder and of flowing water. The storytelling ending 〜のでありました gives it a fairy-tale tone; historical kana: あつて = あって, ゐる = いる, くつきり = くっきり, 今迄 = 今まで.

poems.title: 素朴な琴
poems.author: 八木重吉
poems.paraphrase: この明るい光の中に、一つの素朴な琴を置いたら、秋の美しさに耐えられなくなって、琴はひとりでに静かに鳴り出すだろう。
poems.gloss: If I placed a simple koto in this brightness, unable to bear the beauty of autumn, the koto would quietly begin to play by itself.
poems.note: The whole poem is one sentence: autumn is so beautiful that even an instrument would sound on its own. 〜かね (耐えかね) means 'unable to', and 鳴りいだす is a literary form of 鳴り出す.

poems.title: 秋のひかり
poems.author: 八木重吉
poems.paraphrase: 光がこぼれて落ちてくる。秋の光は地面に落ちて、広がっていく。この光の中で遊ぼう。
poems.gloss: Light comes spilling down. Autumn light falls to the ground and spreads. Let us play in this light.
poems.note: A three-line poem that treats light like water spilling and spreading on the ground. The volitional 遊ぼう ('let's play') turns the image into a gentle invitation.

poems.title: 雪
poems.author: 三好達治

vocabulary.gloss: to come visiting (historical kana for たずね寄る)
to listen (old form of 聴く)

poems.paraphrase:
十一月の夜のあいだずっと、雪が降る、雪が降る。
黄色いランプの光がもれている私の窓に、雪の子どもたちがたずねてくる。
小さな手がガラス戸をたたく。ガラス戸をたたく。たたく。そうしてそこで息が絶える。
私は聞く。彼らの歌の静けさを。静けさ、静けさを。
poems.gloss: All through the November night, snow falls, snow falls. To my window, where the yellow lamplight leaks out, the snow children come visiting. Their small hands knock on the glass door, knock on the glass door, knock, and there they die away. I listen: the stillness of their song, stillness, stillness.
poems.note: Snowflakes are pictured as children who knock on the window and 'die' as they melt against the glass. The text uses old kanji forms (窗 = 窓, 聽 = 聴, 靜 = 静) and historical kana (たづね = たずね, さうして = そうして).

poems.title: 雪
poems.author: 山村暮鳥

vocabulary.gloss: pure white (small っ written as full つ)
what would we do? (historical kana for どうしましょう)
came falling (small っ written as full つ)

poems.paraphrase: きれいな、きれいな雪だなあ。畑も屋根も真っ白だ。きれいでなかったら困ってしまう。だって、空から降ってきた雪なのだから。
poems.gloss: What beautiful, beautiful snow! The fields and the roofs are all white. How could it not be beautiful? It is snow that fell from heaven.
poems.note: A childlike voice delighting in snow; 〜だこと is an exclamation ('what ...!'). きれいでなくつてどうしませう is a rhetorical question meaning 'of course it is beautiful'.

poems.title: 冬の木木
poems.author: 山村暮鳥

vocabulary.gloss: since (winter) has come / even though (literary とて)
coming down (small っ written as full つ)

poems.paraphrase: 冬が来たので、木ははだかだ。春になるまで、木ははだかだ。ちらちらと雪が降ってきて、木は花を着物のように着るけれど、その雪が消えると、また、はだかだ。
poems.gloss: Winter has come, so the trees are bare. Until spring comes, the trees are bare. Snow comes down in flakes, and they wear flowers as their clothes, but when the snow melts away, they are bare again.
poems.note: Snow on bare branches is seen as flowers the trees wear like a kimono. とて after きた is literary and can be read as 'because' or 'even though'; either way the trees stay bare.

poems.title: 冬の長門峡
poems.author: 中原中也

vocabulary.gloss: Nagato Gorge (a gorge in Yamaguchi Prefecture)

poems.paraphrase:
長門峡に、水が流れていた。寒い寒い日だった。
私は料亭にいた。酒をついで飲んでいた。
私のほかに、客は一人もいなかった。
水は、まるで魂があるもののように、流れ流れていた。
やがて、みかんのような色の夕日が、手すりにこぼれ落ちた。
ああ、そんな時もあった。寒い寒い日だった。
poems.gloss: At Nagato Gorge, the water was flowing. It was a cold, cold day. I was at a restaurant, pouring and drinking sake. Apart from me, there were no other guests. The water, just like something with a soul, kept flowing and flowing. Before long, a sunset like a mandarin orange spilled onto the railing. Ah, there was such a time, too. It was a cold, cold day.
poems.note: A quiet, grieving memory of drinking alone by a winter gorge. It uses classical past endings: 〜けり (past with a sense of realization), 〜き (plain recalled past), 〜ぬ and 〜たり (completed action).

poems.title: 雪の宵
poems.author: 中原中也
poems.paraphrase:
(白秋の詩から:青い帽子に降る雪は、過ぎ去ったあの手だろうか、ささやきだろうか。)
ホテルの屋根に降る雪は、過ぎ去ったあの人の手だろうか、ささやきだろうか。
ふかふかと煙突が煙をはいて、赤い火の粉もはね上がる。
今夜の空は真っ暗で、その暗い空から雪が降ってくる。
本当に、別れたあの女は、今ごろどうしているのだろう。
本当に、別れたあの女は、そのうち帰ってくるのだろうか。
私は静かに酒を飲み、後悔ばかりで心が落ち着かない。
静かに静かに酒を飲んで、いとしい思いに心がかき立てられる。
ホテルの屋根に降る雪は、過ぎ去ったあの人の手だろうか、ささやきだろうか。
ふかふかと煙突が煙をはいて、赤い火の粉もはね上がる。
poems.gloss: (Epigraph from Hakushu: The snow falling on a blue soft hat - is it a hand from the past, or a whisper?) The snow falling on the hotel roof - is it that hand from the past, or a whisper? Puffing out smoke, the chimney breathes, and red sparks leap up. Tonight the sky is pitch dark, and from the dark sky falls snow... Truly, that woman I parted from - what is she doing now? Truly, that woman I parted from - will she come back someday? Quietly I drink my sake, restless with regret upon regret. Quietly, quietly I drink, stirred by tender longing. The snow falling on the hotel roof - is it that hand from the past, or a whisper? Puffing out smoke, the chimney breathes, and red sparks leap up.
poems.note: Opens with two lines by Kitahara Hakushu (ソフト is a soft felt hat) and answers them with a snowy night of drinking and missing a lost lover. 過ぎし uses the classical past き, and そそらるる is a classical passive ('to be stirred'); をんな and しづか are historical kana.

poems.title: 永訣の朝
poems.author: 宮沢賢治

vocabulary.gloss: far away (historical kana for とおく)
bullet (historical kana for てっぽうだま)
happiness, good fortune (historical kana for さいわい)

poems.paraphrase:
今日のうちに遠くへ行ってしまう私の妹よ。みぞれが降って、外は妙に明るい。(雨雪を取ってきてちょうだい、と妹は方言で頼む。)うす赤く暗い雲から、みぞれがびしょびしょ降ってくる。青いじゅんさいの模様がある二つの欠けた茶わんに、お前が食べる雪を取ろうとして、私は曲がった鉄砲玉のように暗いみぞれの中へ飛び出した。
ああ、とし子。死ぬという今になって、私を一生明るくするために、お前はこんなさっぱりした雪を一わん頼んだのだ。ありがとう、けなげな妹よ。私もまっすぐに進んでいくから。お前は激しい熱と苦しい息の中から、空から落ちた最後の雪を頼んだのだ。
二つの石の上に、みぞれがさびしくたまっている。私はその上にあぶなく立ち、松の枝から冷たいしずくをたたえた雪を取って、妹の最後の食べ物にしよう。一緒に育ってきた茶わんの藍の模様とも、今日お前は別れてしまう。(私は私で一人で行きます、と妹は言う。)
閉ざされた病室で青白く燃えている、けなげな妹よ。この雪はどこを選んでも真っ白だ。あんなに恐ろしい空から、この美しい雪が来たのだ。(今度生まれてくるときは、こんなに自分のことばかりで苦しまないように生まれてきます、と妹は言う。)
お前が食べるこの二わんの雪に、私は心から祈る。これが天上のアイスクリームになって、お前とみんなに清い糧をもたらすように。私のすべての幸せをかけて願う。
poems.gloss: My little sister, who will go far away before today is over: sleet is falling, and outside it is strangely bright. ('Please get me some rain-snow,' she asks in dialect.) From pale red, gloomier clouds the sleet comes splashing down. Meaning to fetch the snow you will eat in these two chipped earthenware bowls with their blue water-shield pattern, I rushed out into this dark sleet like a bent bullet. From bismuth-colored dark clouds the sleet sinks, splashing. Ah, Toshiko: now, at the moment of dying, you asked me for a bowl of this fresh, clean snow so as to brighten my whole life. Thank you, my brave sister. I too will go straight ahead. Out of your violent fever and gasping, you asked me for the last bowl of snow fallen from the sky of a world called the Milky Way, the sun, the atmosphere. On two blocks of granite the sleet gathers lonely. Standing unsteadily on them, keeping to the pure white two-phase system of snow and water, I will take my gentle sister's last food from this glossy pine branch full of clear cold drops. Today you part from the indigo pattern of the familiar teacup we grew up with. ('I will go on alone, by myself.') Truly today you part from it. Ah, in that closed sickroom, behind the dark screen and mosquito net, gently and palely burning, my brave little sister. This snow is all too white wherever I choose. From that frightening, disordered sky came this beautiful snow. ('If I am born again, I will be born so that I do not suffer only for my own sake like this.') Over these two bowls of snow you will eat, I now pray from my heart: may this become heavenly ice cream and bring you and everyone holy nourishment. I stake all my happiness on this wish.
poems.note: The poet fetches sleet for his dying sister Toshiko; the lines in parentheses are her words in Iwate dialect (あめゆじゆとてちてけんじや 'please get me some rain-snow'; Ora Orade Shitori egumo 'I will go alone, on my own'; the final one 'next time I will be born so as not to suffer only for myself'). The poem is almost entirely in historical kana (けふ = きょう, いつて = いって, ゐる = いる, さいはひ = さいわい).

poems.title: 雨の歌
poems.author: 山村暮鳥

vocabulary.gloss: let's listen (historical kana for 聴こう)
that's it (historical kana for そうだ)
please fall, pour down (small っ as full つ)

poems.paraphrase: 雨が降る。雨が降る。さびしい雨の音でも聞こうか。いや、いや、そうだ。むちで打つように、けるように、強く、強く、激しく、強く、激しく降ってくれ。
poems.gloss: Rain is falling, rain is falling. Shall I listen to the lonely raindrops? No, no - that's it: as if whipping, as if kicking, strongly, strongly, violently, strongly, violently, pour down!
poems.note: The speaker rejects a sad, gentle rain and calls for a fierce one, as if wanting to be shaken awake. Historical kana: 聴かう = 聴こう, さうだ = そうだ, ふつて = ふって.

poems.title: 六月の雨
poems.author: 中原中也

vocabulary.gloss: for a while, a spell (of rain)
appearing (historical kana for たちあらわれて)
sorrow, gloom (historical kana for うれい)

poems.paraphrase:
また少しのあいだ、午前の雨が降る。しょうぶの色のような緑色の雨だ。目のうるんだ、面長の女の人が現れて、消えていく。
現れて消えていくと、雨は悲しみに沈み、しとしとと畑の上に落ちている。いつ終わるともわからず落ちている。
太鼓をたたいて、笛を吹いて、無邪気な子どもが日曜日に畳の上で遊んでいる。
太鼓をたたいて、笛を吹いて遊んでいると、雨が降る。格子窓の外に雨が降る。
poems.gloss: Once more, for a while, the morning rain falls, green like the color of irises. A long-faced woman with moist eyes appears and fades away. As she appears and fades away, the rain, sunk in sorrow, falls softly on the fields, falls without end. Beating a drum and blowing a flute, an innocent child plays on the tatami on a Sunday. While the child plays, beating the drum and blowing the flute, rain falls - rain falls outside the lattice window.
poems.note: The rain is pictured as a sad woman who appears and vanishes, contrasted with a child playing indoors. Note the ruby readings 眼 = まなこ and 女 = ひと, and historical kana うれひ = うれい, ゐる = いる.

poems.title: 時雨
poems.author: 山村暮鳥

vocabulary.gloss: go home! (historical kana for かえれ)
passing shower of late autumn or early winter
mountain pass (historical kana for とうげ)

poems.paraphrase: カラスよ、カラスよ、巣に帰りなさい。峠のしぐれがやって来た。スズメも竹やぶへ帰りなさい。峠のしぐれがやって来た。
poems.gloss: Crow, crow, go back to your nest: the shower from the mountain pass has come. Sparrows, go back too, to the bamboo thicket: the shower from the pass has come.
poems.note: A children's-song style warning to the birds as a cold shower comes down from the pass. The same word appears in kanji (峠) and in historical kana (たうげ = とうげ), a nice reading drill.

poems.title: 庭園の雨
poems.author: 北原白秋
poems.paraphrase:
青い松の葉に、しとしとと雨が降る。すさまじい嵐のあとに、針のように雨が降る。
黄色い毛虫は土にへばりつき、月見草はしおれて白くなっている。
キリ、モミ、イチジク、人が作った盆栽の梅は、けがされた少女のように、みな泣き伏して声も出さない。
しとしとと雨が降る。浜の砂は庭に吹き散らされ、陸橋の下では傷ついた犬がじっと目をこらしている。
あまりにも静かだ。ただ、腹を切った苦しさに肩衣をはねのけた瀬尾のように、あの青い松がふるえている。
こうして一日じゅう、針のように雨が降る。海が見える涼み台の屋根の端に、光ったり、うす暗くなったりする。
雨は降る、しとしとと。雨はやむ、またしばらくのあいだ。夕方になると、血のような虹が、ついにまた海と空にかかる。
poems.gloss: On the green pine needles, rain falls softly. After a terrible storm, rain falls like needles. A yellow caterpillar clings to the soil; the evening primroses have wilted white. The paulownia, the fir, the fig, and the plum trained as a bonsai all lie weeping without a sound, like young girls who have been violated. Softly the rain falls. Sand from the beach is blown across the garden, and under the bridge an injured dog stares intently. It is too quiet; only the green pine trembles, like Senoo throwing off his ceremonial shoulder-robe in the agony of cutting open his belly. And so, all day long, the rain falls like needles on the gable of the cool-air platform that looks out to sea, now shining, now dim. The rain falls softly; the rain stops, for a little while again. When evening comes, a rainbow like blood hangs at last once more between the sea and the sky.
poems.note: A garden battered by a storm, described through violent images; 瀬尾 is probably a samurai character from a kabuki play who dies by seppuku, but the reference is not certain. Classical forms: 〜き/〜し (凄まじき, 犯されし) are attributive endings, 〜なり means 'is', 見ゆる means 'can be seen', and をぐらく (小暗く) means 'dim'.

poems.title: 〔雨ニモマケズ〕
poems.author: 宮沢賢治

vocabulary.gloss: to be (historical kana for いる)

poems.paraphrase:
雨にも負けず、風にも負けず、雪にも夏の暑さにも負けない、じょうぶな体を持つ。欲はなく、決して怒らず、いつも静かに笑っている。一日に玄米四合と、みそと少しの野菜を食べる。どんなことも、自分を勘定に入れずに、よく見て聞いて理解し、そして忘れない。野原の松林のかげの、小さなかやぶきの小屋にいる。
東に病気の子どもがいれば、行って看病してやる。西に疲れた母がいれば、行ってその稲の束を背負う。南に死にそうな人がいれば、行って、怖がらなくてもいいと言う。北にけんかや訴訟があれば、つまらないからやめろと言う。ひでりの時は涙を流し、寒い夏はおろおろ歩く。みんなにでくのぼうと呼ばれ、ほめられもせず、苦にもされない。そういう者に、私はなりたい。
(最後に、法華経の仏や菩薩の名を唱える言葉が並んでいる。)
poems.gloss: Not beaten by the rain, not beaten by the wind, not beaten by snow or by the summer heat, with a sturdy body, without greed, never getting angry, always quietly smiling. Eating four go of brown rice a day, with miso and a few vegetables. In all things, not counting myself in, seeing, hearing and understanding well, and not forgetting. Living in a small grass-thatched hut in the shade of the pine grove on the plain. If there is a sick child to the east, going and nursing him; if there is a tired mother to the west, going and carrying her bundles of rice; if there is someone about to die to the south, going and telling him he need not be afraid; if there is a quarrel or a lawsuit to the north, telling them to stop because it is pointless. In a drought, shedding tears; in a cold summer, walking about at a loss. Called a blockhead by everyone, neither praised nor a bother to anyone: that is the kind of person I want to become. (The text ends with invocations to the Buddha, bodhisattvas and the Lotus Sutra.)
poems.note: Written in katakana with kanji like a private notebook entry; ズ/ヌ are classical negatives, ヰ = い, and ケンクヮ = けんか. ヒドリ is debated: it is usually taken as 日照り 'drought', but some read it as 日取り 'day labor'; 朿 in the text is taken as 束 'bundle'.
